samples.summary: New observable API side effect (insert/delete can grow the freeze pane past a straddling merge) is documented only in the controller TSDoc; the user-facing REST docs and docs/design/rest-api.md still describe the old contract
samples.evidence: `shiftWorksheetViewState` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:278) now snaps `frozenRows`/`frozenCols` past any straddling merge, so `POST .../insert` and `POST .../delete` can return with a larger frozen band than the band adjustment alone implies — and a row-axis edit can even change `frozenCols`. The controller TSDoc was updated (packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-structure.controller.ts:63-72), but packages/documentation/developers/rest-api.md:556-566 still says only that "the index-keyed view state (… freeze pane) follow[s] the edit" plus "two deliberate differences from the editor", and docs/design/rest-api.md:282-320 likewise lists only the cleared-formula-values and the move-409 differences. API consumers (and the CLI, packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-structure.ts:117/167, which proxies these endpoints verbatim) have no documented reason to re-read `GET .../freeze` after a structural edit.

finding.summary: REST insert/delete still leaves merges straddling the freeze — the new invariant's remaining door
finding.evidence: The change establishes "no merged block may straddle a frozen boundary" and closes the editor paths (`Sheet.moveCells`, `moveRangeTo`, `planPasteMerges`) plus, on the API, `POST .../move` (`assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze`) and `PUT .../merges` / `PUT .../freeze`. `Sheet.shiftCells` additionally snaps the boundary after an insert/delete (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1415-1429). The backend's shared insert/delete path does not: `applyShift` at packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-structure.controller.ts:322-360 calls `applyWorksheetShift` and nothing else — the helper adjusts `frozenRows`/`frozenCols` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:246-265) but never runs `snapFreezePastMerges` or `crossesFreezePane`. So `POST .../insert` (or `delete`) on a tab with a frozen band and a merged block below/inside it can still persist the exact straddling, unpaintable state the rest of the change works to make unreachable, and the engine only repairs it if a later local `shiftCells` happens to run (`loadMerges`/`loadFreezePane` do not snap — see the test at packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts:835 which seeds precisely this state). Fix belongs in `applyShift` (or inside `applyWorksheetShift`, which would also cover the frontend store path).

verdict.reason: The finding claims `applyWorksheetShift` never runs `snapFreezePastMerges`, leaving the REST insert/delete path (`applyShift`) able to persist a merge straddling the freeze. That is false here. `applyWorksheetShift` calls `shiftWorksheetViewState` (worksheet-structure.ts:611) after `replaceMerges` (:598), and `shiftWorksheetViewState` ends by calling `snapFreezePastMerges(ws.merges, ws.frozenRows, ws.frozenCols)` and writing the snapped values back (worksheet-structure.ts:271-288), with the helper imported at :18 from model/worksheet/merging.ts:197-207. The controller's `applyShift` routes both POST insert and POST delete through that same helper (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:330-362), so the snap is applied on the REST path — and, because it lives inside the shared helper, on the frontend YorkieStore path (yorkie-store.ts:480-498) as well, which is exactly the fix the finding asks for. Dedicated tests assert it: worksheet-structure.test.ts:198-220 seeds frozenRows=3 with A3:A5, inserts a row, and expects frozenRows===6; :222-237 asserts a non-straddling freeze is left alone. Since the guard is not missing, there is no bypassing call site to block on.
